title: 1925 Portuguese legislative election
summary: The election of 8 November 1925 gave the Democratic Party 83 of the 163 seats in the Chamber and 39 of the 70 in the Senate, under the incomplete-list system that reserved part of each circle to the minorities. It was the last election held under the constitution of 1911 and the last multi-party election in Portugal until the Constituent Assembly of April 1975 — fifty years, to within six months. The parliament it returned lasted six months: the column that left Braga on 28 May 1926 dissolved it, and nothing elected replaced it until 1934, when a single list did. It is in the atlas as the parliament the coup swept away.
